prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop landing-page first viewport decision comp
Primary request: Create a shippable-looking 16:10 desktop homepage comp for Orifude in a “Literary Sunday edition” direction. It should feel like an independent literary review or beautifully art-directed Sunday books supplement: quiet, generous, human, intelligent, tactile, and unmistakably editorial. This is a real product website, not concept art.
Input images: Image 1 is the supplied Orifude wordmark; preserve its exact identity and use it once, small and crisp in the masthead. Image 2 is the supplied squirrel courier cutout; preserve it and use it once, sparingly, as a small delivery punctuation near the terminal proof. Image 3 is a real Orifude terminal recording frame; reproduce this exact frame as the hero’s product proof rather than inventing terminal content.
Scene/backdrop: a full browser viewport on warm uncoated paper #fbf7f1 with barely perceptible natural fiber, no browser chrome. Ink #292823 dominates.
Composition/framing: exact 16:10 landscape desktop viewport, designed at 1600×1000. A slim but spacious masthead across the top with the supplied wordmark at left and three plain text links at right: “How it works”, “Privacy”, “Download”. Below, one large asymmetrical editorial opening with broad margins and a strong two-column rhythm. The left editorial column occupies about 48% and carries the headline with exceptionally generous leading and whitespace. The right column is one large, real-looking terminal recording image, using Image 3 as the exact evidence, set with the directness of a full-bleed review photograph or printed plate, not inside a rounded card. Let it overlap the editorial grid slightly, but never obscure copy. A restrained moss vertical block or broad crop may anchor the proof, but do not frame every element. At the very bottom edge, hint at the next section with one substantial serif line, not cards.
Text, verbatim and highly legible:
“Send a letter into the quiet.”
“Orifude carries one private letter to one unrelated stranger. They may send one reply. Then the exchange becomes a keepsake.”
“Download v0.2.0”
“See how it works”
“Private alpha. Online access is invite-only.”
“ONE LETTER. ONE STRANGER. ONE REPLY.”
Typography: large literary serif display face with the conviction and readability of a serious independent review, paired with a warm highly legible humanist sans for factual copy. Headline should be very large, approximately 88–108 px, balanced over three lines, dark ink, with no italic gimmick and no ultra-thin strokes. Body copy at a comfortably readable 20–23 px. Use monospace only inside the real terminal image. No eyebrow above the headline.
Color palette: warm paper #fbf7f1, soft ink #292823, muted moss #858a72, restrained ember #a45b52. Moss appears mainly on the primary download action and one substantial editorial accent. Ember appears only as a tiny status or printer’s mark. Avoid neutral gray and pure black except the dark terminal proof.
Materials/textures: fine uncoated book paper, subtle ink absorption, one broad rule or paper edge at most; premium print restraint rather than scrapbook collage.
Details: primary action is a decisive moss-colored rectangular editorial button with sharp or subtly clipped paper corners, large enough to read. Secondary action is a plain underlined text link. The small courier from Image 2 appears once near the transition into the recording, no larger than needed. The terminal proof must look like a real screen recording frame with the exact warm-on-charcoal text and hierarchy of Image 3. Preserve honest product positioning and do not imply a browser letter client.
Constraints: full-fidelity professional landing page; exact supplied wordmark and squirrel identity; real terminal image as proof; headline exactly “Send a letter into the quiet.”; restrained spot color; strong readable type; generous negative space; coherent desktop UI; no invented testimonials, logos, statistics, awards, customer claims, or end-to-end-encryption claims; no watermark.
Avoid: no thin-line border soup, no glows, no glassmorphism, no gradients, no rounded-card grid, no stack of cards, no dashboard aesthetic, no fake browser or fake terminal controls, no excessive monospace, no tiny labels, no all-caps overload, no Japanese pastiche, no origami collage, no decorative branch sprawling across the page, no centered generic SaaS hero, no split-screen template feeling.
